nodes.label: Separate home and party views
nodes.rationale: Home provides Create and Join tiles; the party view groups the shared screen, source selection, room details and chat. Native dialogs provide room creation/joining, party menu, help and invitation surfaces.

nodes.label: Accessible party-chat markup
nodes.rationale: Chat provides a focusable polite live log, empty state, unread-message button, labeled textarea, count, send button and expandable emoji picker. Controls begin disabled before a room is joined. The displayed limit is 1,000 while textarea maxlength is 2,000 UTF-16 units.

nodes.label: Room code, participants and LAN invitation UI
nodes.norm_label: room code, participants and lan invitation ui
nodes.rationale: Room panels and party menu expose codes and participant lists. The invitation dialog selects among reachable network addresses and copies an invite link; help instructs guests to share the local network and keep the host server running.

nodes.label: Shared player and custom transport surface
nodes.norm_label: shared player and custom transport surface
nodes.rationale: The party UI supplies local and YouTube player containers, host-labeled playback/seek controls, viewer-local audio and fullscreen controls, a user-gesture playback gate and visible player error/retry controls.

nodes.label: Video upload and YouTube source forms
nodes.norm_label: video upload and youtube source forms
nodes.rationale: Source controls include MP4/WebM/OGV file selection, upload progress and cancellation, and a YouTube URL form. Markup advertises the default 2 GB limit.

nodes.label: Keyboard, hidden and reduced-motion states
nodes.rationale: Visible keyboard focus, disabled control states, a visually-hidden utility, an explicit hidden-element rule and reduced-motion scroll behavior support the interactive page surfaces.

nodes.label: Scrollable responsive chat and emoji styling
nodes.norm_label: scrollable responsive chat and emoji styling
nodes.rationale: A fixed-height flex panel gives the message log independent scrolling. Pre-wrapped text and overflow wrapping handle multiline/long messages; own-message styling distinguishes the sender. The emoji picker uses seven columns and emoji font fallbacks; mobile rules enlarge composition text and emoji options.

nodes.label: White-paper and black-ink design tokens
nodes.rationale: CSS variables define paper, ink, gray rules/wash and system monospace, serif and body fonts. Borders, typography, outlines and restrained grayscale states implement the monochrome visual direction.

nodes.label: Responsive home and party layouts
nodes.rationale: Desktop party layout uses a flexible screen column and fixed-width room column. Breakpoints reduce spacing and column widths; at 650 pixels home tiles and workspace become single-column and the player changes to 4:3. Smaller layouts adjust typography and hide selected secondary details.

nodes.label: YouTube IFrame API playback
nodes.rationale: Each guest streams directly from YouTube. Embedding requires internet access and an HTTP-served page; unavailable videos, embedding restrictions, loading failures and autoplay restrictions have visible handling.

nodes.label: Watch Party LAN prototype
nodes.rationale: Host-run LAN watch party using plain HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript with Node.js, Express, Socket.IO and HTTP video streaming. No frontend build step or database.

nodes.label: White rounded square with dark border
nodes.norm_label: white rounded square with dark border

nodes.label: Server-authoritative playback commands
nodes.rationale: Only the host may play, pause, seek or select sources, with server-side validation. Commands are ordered, per-video IDs reject controls for replaced sources, and snapshots restore late arrivals or reconnects. Volume, mute and fullscreen are local controls.

nodes.label: Room-scoped chat protocol
nodes.rationale: Separate Socket.IO chat events avoid changing playback or rebroadcasting full video state. Membership is required and sender identity comes from the server session. Plain-text messages allow 1,000 Unicode code points and six accepted messages per participant per five seconds. Each room retains 100 messages and 400 accepted IDs for retry deduplication; page-local drafts survive connection loss.

nodes.label: Deferred features and performance work
nodes.rationale: Discovery, recommendations, filters/search, standalone reactions, playlists, polls, continuous drift correction, clock synchronization and latency optimization are deferred. The edition claims neither p99 latency nor drift targets.

nodes.label: Persistent LAN host server
nodes.rationale: Guests use a reachable LAN address on the same network. The original server computer must remain running even after browser closure or host-role transfer; transferring the host role does not move the server or uploaded files.

nodes.label: Server-timestamp playback anchor
nodes.rationale: Play, pause and seek update a server-time anchor so late arrivals receive the calculated current position. Clients do not continuously correct playback; buffering, ads, suspended tabs and network delay can cause drift.

nodes.label: Invite-prototype media access control
nodes.rationale: Uploads require the connected host's room token and media access requires a participant token. Public snapshots omit tokens and upload paths. Room codes are invitations rather than passwords; public deployment requires HTTPS, user authentication, storage quotas and deployment hardening.

nodes.label: Room membership and host lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Rooms use six-character codes or invites and allow 20 members including disconnected sessions. Host disconnection reserves the role for 20 seconds before online failover; explicit leave transfers immediately. Reconnect sessions last ten minutes, explicit leave removes a session, and empty rooms expire. In-memory rooms, messages and sessions are lost on restart.

nodes.label: Authenticated HTTP uploaded-video delivery
nodes.rationale: MP4, WebM and OGV uploads travel through multipart HTTP and stream from local disk with HTTP range support rather than through Socket.IO. Default upload limit is 2 GB; no transcoding occurs. Replaced sources and expired rooms trigger cleanup; graceful shutdown removes the process upload directory, while crashes can leave files behind.

nodes.label: Physical-device LAN acceptance checklist
nodes.rationale: Pending manual acceptance covers reachable LAN invites, real playable media, late joins/reconnects, host transfer, autoplay and embed failures, ten actual browser participants, guest permissions, failure recovery, mobile/keyboard use and chat interactions. Protocol tests cannot establish ten-stream capacity; latency and player drift require a separate physical-device benchmark.

nodes.label: Original-layout two-tab browser verification
nodes.rationale: The original interface was checked with two independent browser tabs for room creation, invitation joins, refresh restoration, host transfer, local WebM, shared playback commands, YouTube and disabled guest controls. A 375-pixel guest viewport had no horizontal overflow. These checks apply to the original interface.

nodes.label: Thirteen HTTP and Socket.IO integration tests
nodes.norm_label: thirteen http and socket.io integration tests
nodes.rationale: Tests run on one Windows computer with Node.js 24.16.0 using real loopback sockets. Ten-user checks mean one host and nine protocol clients, not ten decoding players or physical devices. Synthetic upload bytes verify streaming and authorization rather than decoding. Six chat cases bring the suite to thirteen tests and check that messaging preserves playback sequence and revision.

nodes.label: Revised layout and chat browser-verification gap
nodes.norm_label: revised layout and chat browser-verification gap
nodes.rationale: The e-ink revision and chat have passing integration/syntax checks, and static checks resolve page references, SVG symbols and labels. Browser security policy blocked visual/interaction inspection of the revised layout; the chat panel and emoji picker remain visually unverified. Normal-browser checks are still required.
